purpose: Separate native gameplay correctness from inactive host CoreAudio mixing and audio playback teardown.
rendering: Native macOS Metal / Forward+ window for all attached probes; not headless.
observations: 22 real production vehicle engines with default CoreAudio and normal rendering produced no observed mix boundaries during a 1000 ms bounded observation; all 22 AudioStreamPlaybackWAV and associated 22 AudioStreamWAV objects remained referenced at exit.
The corresponding 22-vehicle Dummy-driver probe observed three mix boundaries in 205 ms after stop and stream clearing; exit reported no leaked objects. Dummy produces no audible output.
A minimal SceneTree loading no game scripts, creating one AudioStreamPlayer and one synthetic WAV, observed zero CoreAudio mix boundaries during 3000 ms and two leaked objects at exit.
The unchanged final release App reproduced 44 WAV/playback leaks while passing all 40 survival gameplay checks.

Restoring normal rendering, explicitly drawing frames, removing fixed FPS, and selecting the existing default speaker within the test process did not restore host CoreAudio mixing. No operating-system output preference was changed.

Dummy with only the original five process frames after stop also leaked 44 WAV/playback objects: 0.627 ms elapsed, less than the reported 40 ms until its next mix. The zero-leak Dummy case explicitly observed three mix boundaries after stopping, so selecting Dummy alone is insufficient.
Headless vehicle fixtures are not an audio teardown comparison: production harbor_vehicle._setup_audio() returns immediately for a headless DisplayServer and creates no engine playback.
limits: These measurements do not identify why CoreAudio failed to mix on this host.
No engine or production audio fix is claimed; normal release audio defaults remain unchanged.
No human listening verification was performed. A Dummy-driver native validation cannot verify audible CoreAudio output.
The two 22-vehicle log commands differ in audio driver and an extra pre-stop manual draw in the CoreAudio case; both enabled normal rendering and measured mix boundaries after stopping playback.
Absolute local user/project/temp paths in logs are replaced with named placeholders; warning and leak lines are retained.

confirmed_chain: _mix_step (489-493) invokes deletion registration. _delete_stream_playback_list_node (673-680) registers a main-thread destructor that releases stream_playback.
update (1505) and cleanup (1511) process already registered deletions; they cannot replace an absent mixer step.
CoreAudio.start (246-254) calls AudioOutputUnitStart and reports an error on failure; these logs contain no such failure message. The cause of absent callbacks remains unverified.
No script API for flush, force_mix or restart is exposed.

shutdown_contract_follow_up.production_change: Shutdown now stops and clears each audio stream, watches only weak playback references and waits until all are released or a real wall-clock 1000 ms deadline expires. No audio driver changes or warning filters.
shutdown_contract_follow_up.host_state_changed: CoreAudio later resumed mixing without changing operating-system settings. The earlier zero-mix results remain historical observations, not a claim about current device state.
shutdown_contract_follow_up.results: Both drivers completed the native 22-vehicle and plain/2D playback regression with zero leaked objects. Expired-deadline handling is independently exercised without disabling mixing or keeping a strong playback reference.
shutdown_contract_follow_up.inactive_coreaudio_timeout_not_reproduce: An explicit --expect-timeout invocation instead observed actual mix and completed playback release in 10 ms. This environmental precondition was no longer present; no inactive-device recovery is claimed.

publication_note: Sanitized log bytes retained; .log suffix renamed .txt for the public source allowlist.
